requirement:
Each prose paragraph has an anonymous `paragraph` node under its nearest
enclosing outline container. This includes paragraphs before the first heading
and inside list items, quotations, and directive bodies. Their selectors follow
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Heading text and literal
code-block contents create no paragraph nodes.
rationale:
No test verifies `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.paragraphs`. `references` returns no impl, test or cite sites for it, and the mandatory inputs include no test source. The requirement has no {fixme} acknowledgment.

I searched the crates for "paragraph". The only hits are in `crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline/tests.rs`:
- `reflowing_markdown_paragraphs_keeps_the_hash` is about structural hashing.
- `markdown_hashes_include_paragraph_text_between_punctuation_tokens` is also about hashing.
- `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` is about comment handling.

None of them is marked {test} for this requirement. None asserts that paragraph nodes exist or where they sit in the outline.

The markdown book also says the paragraph contract is "not yet implemented" in `md/requirements/sdk/sources/markdown.md`. I relied on that book text and did not read the implementation.

The obligations below are untested, and none qualifies for a testing exemption:
- Each prose paragraph produces an anonymous `paragraph` node.
- The node sits under its nearest enclosing outline container.
- Paragraphs before the first heading are covered.
- Paragraphs inside list items, quotations and directive bodies are covered.
- Selectors follow `requirements.references.outline_selectors`, so each is `paragraph@hash` with `#N` disambiguation.
- Heading text creates no paragraph node.
- Literal code-block contents create no paragraph node.

An implementation that emitted no paragraph nodes, nested them under the wrong container, or created them for headings or code blocks would pass every reviewed test.

text: Each prose paragraph has an anonymous `paragraph` node under its nearest
enclosing outline container. This includes paragraphs before the first heading
and inside list items, quotations, and directive bodies. Their selectors follow
code-block contents create no paragraph nodes.
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
